data.title: Seegnal Inc. Announces Q3 Filing Exemption and Appointment of a Special Committee to Review Strategic Alternatives
data.description:
CALGARY, AB, Nov. 20, 2026 /CNW/ -- Seegnal Inc. () (FSE: 2I1) ("Seegnal" or the "Company"), a developer of innovative healthcare technology focused on mitigating medication risks, announces the adoption of semi-annual financial reporting. This news release is being filed pursuant to Coordinated Blanket Order 51 – 933 Exemptions to Permit Semi-Annual Reporting for Certain Venture Issuers ("CBO 51-933").

CBO 51-933 allows eligible venture issuers to voluntarily move from a quarterly to a semi-annual financial reporting framework. Seegnal's fiscal year ends on December 31. Under the provisions of CBO 51-933, Seegnal will be exempt from the requirements to file its nine-month interim financial statements and associated management's discussion and analysis ("MD&A") as it meets the eligibility criteria under CBO 51-933, which include being a venture issuer with annual revenues of less than $10 million and maintaining a clean 12-month continuous disclosure record. Accordingly, Seegnal will not be filing its interim financial statements for the nine-month period ending September 30, 2026 and associated MD&A.

Seegnal will continue to file audited annual financial statements (due within 120 days of December 31, 2026) and six-month interim financial reports (due next within 60 days of June 30, 2027). Seegnal remains committed to timely disclosure and will continue to report all material changes and significant developments as required under National Instrument 51-102 – Continuous Disclosure Obligations.

Special Committee

The Company's board of directors (the "Board") has established a special committee of independent directors (the "Special Committee") to lead the Company's evaluation of strategic and financing alternatives.

The Special Committee is exploring a full range of options, which may include, but are not limited to, a merger, sale, related party transaction or other alternative. To assist in its work, the Special Committee may engage professional advisors as it considers appropriate, including legal, financial and accounting advisors.

The Board has not set a timetable for this evaluation process, nor has it made any decisions regarding any potential strategic transaction. There can be no assurance that this process will result in any transaction. The Company does not intend to provide updates or make further comments regarding these matters unless and until it determines that additional disclosure is appropriate or required by law. Seegnal cautions that there are no guarantees that the evaluation processes will result in any particular outcome. The Company will continue to operate its business as usual as it undertakes these evaluation processes.

About Seegnal

Seegnal Inc. () (FSE: 2I1) is an innovative healthcare technology company dedicated to reducing medication-related harm where care begins. The Company's SaaS-based clinical decision support platform is designed to help clinicians prescribe with greater precision by integrating patient-specific data at the point of care, including medications, laboratory results, renal function, allergies, age and other relevant risk factors. By delivering more targeted, context-aware medication insights within existing clinical workflows, Seegnal aims to reduce alert fatigue, support safer prescribing and advance a more personalized standard of patient care. Seegnal's technology is deployed across healthcare settings and is used by approximately 15,000 clinicians in daily practice. For additional Company information, please visit https://www.seegnal.com/ and follow us on LinkedIn.

data.title: International Grains Council Raises Wheat Production Forecast, Cuts Corn — Market Talk
data.description: The International Grains Council raised its 2026/27 global production estimate for wheat and coarse grains by 1 million metric tons to 2.428 billion tons, with higher wheat and barley numbers offsetting lower corn. data.title: Praxis a new Buy at B Riley on cusp of potential approval for two therapies
data.description:
Key points:
  • B Riley initiated Praxis Precision Medicines at Buy, saying that the company may soon have two drug approvals in its hands with FDA action dates coming up in December and January for, respectively, relutrigine and ulixacaltamide.
  • The firm has a price target of $713 (~129% upside based on Nov. 19 close).
  • Analyst Madison El-Saadi said that ulixacaltamide, for essential tremor, has blockbuster potential given that the movement disorder is 10 times more prevalent than Parkinson's disease "yet neglected by drug developers for decades."
  • He sees ulixacaltamide achieving a more than $1B annual run rate by the end of 2027, compared to the Street consensus of 2029.
  • El-Saadi has "high conviction" the therapy will be approved by its PDUFA date of Jan. 29, adding he believes that the Street is underestimating ulixacaltamide, as Praxis will have around 300 sales reps targeting around 19,000 prescribers.
  • Relutrigine, which would treat SCN2A/SCN8A developmental and epileptic encephalopathies, has a Dec. 27 PDUFA date. El-Saadi noted that the candidate's chances of approval were bolstered by the registrational cohort of the EMBOLD trial, which was stopped early due to efficacy.

data.title: Can Keto Diet Help Reduce Liver Fat And Control Blood Sugar?
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - A new study suggests that the ketogenic (keto) diet may be better than the Mediterranean and low-fat diets at reducing fat in the liver and improving overall health.

The study included 42 adults who were overweight or obese, had prediabetes and suffered from fatty liver disease. They were divided into three groups, with each group following a different diet. The first group followed a keto diet, which contains very few carbohydrates and more fat. The second followed a Mediterranean diet, which includes a balance of carbohydrates and healthy fats. The third followed a low-fat diet based mainly on plant foods.

To make sure everyone followed their assigned diet, researchers provided all the meals and arranged weekly meetings with a dietitian. The amount of food was adjusted for each person so that everyone could lose about 10% of their starting body weight. This took around four to five months.

At the end of the study, all three groups had lost body fat and showed improvements in how their bodies handled blood sugar. However, the keto group showed the biggest improvement in liver fat.

People following the keto diet had an average 67% reduction in liver fat, while those following the Mediterranean and low-fat diets had a 45% reduction. Researchers also found that people on the keto diet had higher levels of glucagon and lower levels of insulin.

Another interesting finding was that the keto diet helped more people move out of the prediabetes range. By the end of the study, around 50% of people following the keto diet no longer had prediabetes. This was compared with 29% of those following the Mediterranean diet and only 7% of those on the low-fat diet.

More research involving larger groups and longer follow-up periods is needed to find out whether these benefits last.

data.title: US Justice Department drops appeal in Alaska Senate suit
data.description:
By Dan Rosenzweig-Ziff

The US Justice Department dropped its appeal on Thursday in its attempt to block certification of this month's Alaska Senate election after Democratic challenger Mary Peltola secured more than 50% of the vote.

The race was called on Tuesday, two weeks after the election, with the count showing Peltola leading by four percentage points. Peltola's win gave Democrats a 56-44 majority in the Senate.

In a lawsuit filed before the midterms, the Justice Department had sought to preemptively delay certification of the vote so it could probe whether a candidate with a similar name to Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan had led to voter confusion. A federal judge had said the government had no such authority.

In Thursday's filing, Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward asked the appeals court to dismiss the case, as the government "reluctantly" acknowledged that there was no viable path to investigate the vote with the ballots already counted and no longer identifiable.

He also asked the appeals court to vacate the lower court's ruling.

The closely watched Senate race became the subject of controversy after The New York Times reported days before the vote that Peltola's campaign recruited a retired school teacher named Dan J. Sullivan. Peltola has said she had no part in or knowledge of the reported effort.

The government has also launched a criminal probe into whether that recruitment effort was an illegal attempt to confuse voters. DOJ has sent letters to more than 20 people notifying them they are subjects of that probe, Reuters previously reported. Those are among the more than 140 letters, subpoenas and notices DOJ officials have sent. Targets include prominent voting rights lawyer Marc Elias, whose firm has represented Democrats including Peltola.

FBI agents also questioned donors to Dan J. Sullivan ahead of the election, saying they were investigating possible fraud.

data.title: Anthropic retail traders face losses as shares dive 13% the day after debut
data.description:
Key points:
  • $750 million of Anthropic stock traded Thursday, most for any debut, Vanda says
  • Stock opened at $112 on Thursday, fell to $85 Friday
  • Global stocks down on Friday as doubts about AI mount

By Harry Robertson

Retail investors who snapped up Anthropic shares at a near-record pace after its IPO face losses a day later, after the stock dropped 13% in early US trading on Friday, with doubts mounting about the outlook for artificial intelligence.

Anthropic sold 980 million shares at $83 apiece on Thursday in the biggest IPO in history, giving stock market investors the first chance to buy into a frontier AI company.

The retail investors who missed out on the initial offering helped drive the third-biggest day of net retail buying for a stock on its debut on records going back to 2012, according to Vanda Research, and the biggest day of turnover overall.

LSEG data shows that on Thursday, the stock began trading at $112, far above its IPO price, and closed at $97. On Friday, it fell sharply to $85 by 12:20 p.m. ET (1720 GMT), meaning buyers on the secondary market who drove the price up a day earlier were left facing losses.

Vanda Research, which tracks DIY investors, said that overall more than $750 million of Anthropic stock was traded by retail on Thursday, the most for a debut on its records. That compared to $670 million for SpaceX at its IPO in June .

Yet net buying was below SpaceX's IPO record of $118 million and Coinbase's $92 million .

"Different investors are different but most will be willing to look through the short-term volatility and focus on the bigger future," Viraj Patel, global macro strategist at Vanda, said of Anthropic.

One retail investing platform focused on Europe said trading volume, the number of traders and average order size for Anthropic was lower than SpaceX on the first day of trading.

Global stocks fell on Friday as sentiment soured on the AI trade, with investors anxious to see stronger returns for the huge amounts of expenditure on model training and buildout.

Anthropic said less than 20% of shares were allocated to retail investors.

One person involved in the deal said the retail allocation was slightly lower than initially anticipated due to very strong demand from institutional investors.

In the UK, 3.6 million shares worth around $300 million were allocated to retail investors, according to RetailBook, which coordinated the offering.

British investment platform Hargreaves Lansdown said clients received 34% of the shares they requested, in line with other platforms.

data.title: Novo Gets FDA Approval For First-Of-Its-Kind Weekly Growth Hormone Treatment For Children With Turner Syndrome
data.description:
Key points:
  • Over 52 weeks, patients receiving once-weekly Sogroya grew an average of 8.9 cms, compared with 9.7 cms among those receiving daily growth hormone injections.
  • Novo said the results demonstrated comparable growth, with Sogroya providing 313 injection-free days annually.
  • Sogroya is already approved for growth hormone deficiency and Noonan syndrome.

Novo Nordisk (NVO) announced on Friday that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved its once-weekly growth hormone treatment, Sogroya, for children aged 2.5 years and older with growth failure associated with Turner syndrome.

Turner syndrome is a genetic condition affecting around one in 2,000 newborn females, often causing short stature and other developmental complications, according to the company.

NVO shares traded 1.3% lower at the time of writing.

Novo’s Phase 3 Trial Involved 105 Children With Turner Syndrome

The approval makes Sogroya the first and only once-weekly, long-acting growth hormone treatment for the condition, offering an alternative to daily injections.

The approval was supported by Novo’s Phase 3 Real8 trial involving 105 children with Turner syndrome. Over 52 weeks, patients receiving once-weekly Sogroya had an average annualized growth rate of of 8.9 centimeters, compared with 9.7 centimeters among those receiving daily growth hormone injections.

313 Fewer Injections Annually

Novo said the results demonstrated comparable growth between the treatments. “A once-weekly option represents a meaningful advancement in how we support growth in children with Turner Syndrome, reducing the number of injections throughout that journey,” said Colleen Silk, Group VP, Rare Disease, Novo.

Aristides Maniatis, an investigator in the trial, highlighted the convenience of fewer injections, noting that Sogroya provides 313 injection-free days annually. “This weekly alternative to daily therapy may help make the growth hormone routine simpler to fit into the lives of children and their caregivers.”

The approval also expands Sogroya’s existing indications, including growth hormone deficiency and Noonan syndrome, a genetic disorder that can cause short stature, heart defects and other developmental problems.

Retail’s Take On NVO

Retail sentiment surrounding NVO on Stocktwits flipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘bullish’ over the past 24 hours.

NVO shares are down nearly 27% so far in 2026, while rival Eli Lilly (LLY) has gained more than 25%.

data.title: Anthropic at $83 Would Be Trading at a 'Discount,' Analysts Say — WSJ
data.description:
By Telis Demos

As Anthropic shares on Friday tumble back toward their offering price, some investors might be trying to figure if they are buyers again.

William Blair analysts led by Arjun Bhatia on Thursday wrote that at the IPO price of $83 per share, Anthropic is valued at about 9 times the analysts' 2027 revenue estimate of $136 billion.

That ratio is based on an enterprise value, which uses a fully diluted share count and also subtracts out the company's estimated cash at year-end.

At that multiple, it would put Anthropic toward the middle of a range of comparable public companies, with Meta Platforms at around 5 times on that basis, and CrowdStrike at around 36 times, according to the analysts.

At nine times, "we believe the multiple is very reasonable" the analysts wrote. "This is a discount to many other leading tech companies that have much slower growth rates."

The analysts' 2027 sales estimate is in line with other forecasts. Visible Alpha's current analyst consensus is $139 billion, based on five estimates. FactSet puts the consensus at $130 billion.

More analyst estimates will come in once the underwriting banks begin publishing research. That usually happens a few weeks after an IPO.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
